## Cardiac monitoring services

Specialized Medical LLC provides nationwide ambulatory cardiac monitoring services for physician practices, cardiology groups, hospitals and health systems. Supported services include 24–48 hour Holter Monitoring, Long-Term Holter Monitoring for more than 48 hours through 7 days, Extended Holter Monitoring for more than 7 days through 14 days, Cardiac Event Monitoring for 1–30 days and Mobile Cardiac Telemetry (MCT) for 1–30 days.

For supported LIVE STREAMING studies, Specialized Medical can follow operational indicators such as monitor battery, electrode contact, monitor-to-phone Bluetooth connection, phone-to-network cellular connection and successful ECG data transmission. When an operational issue is identified, the team can contact the patient and help troubleshoot. Operational visibility is not the same as a clinical diagnosis or clinical alert.

Holter and longer Holter findings are presented after the final report is generated. Qualifying Event Monitoring and Mobile Cardiac Telemetry findings may be presented during the study according to the ordering physician's prescribed notification protocol, followed by a final report.

Selected 24–48 hour and 3–7 day non-live Holter configurations are available for patients who are unable or unwilling to carry the assigned monitoring phone. These configurations record ECG for later analysis and do not provide live operational test-status visibility during wear.

The assigned monitoring phone connects to the monitor by Bluetooth. Specialized Medical's Always Connected technology supports five cellular networks across two countries: AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon in the United States, and Telcel and AT&T Mexico in Mexico. This expanded connectivity helps maintain live ECG data transmission in supported monitoring configurations, subject to available coverage and network conditions. Connectivity varies with location and network conditions and uninterrupted coverage is not guaranteed.

Specialized Medical provides monitoring technology, operational support, review workflows and communication support. Test selection, interpretation and patient-care decisions remain with the treating physician and healthcare organization.

## Live ECG monitoring

Live ECG monitoring is ambulatory monitoring in which rhythm information is transmitted during the prescribed study instead of waiting for the wearable monitor to be returned. In the Specialized Medical workflow, the wearable communicates with an assigned phone by Bluetooth. The phone transmits available ECG information through cellular service into the monitoring workflow when connectivity is available.

Live transmission depends on monitor operation, electrode contact, Bluetooth connection, phone power and status, cellular-network availability and successful data receipt. The system is designed to reconnect when service becomes available after a temporary interruption. Uninterrupted coverage and instantaneous transmission are not guaranteed.

For supported live configurations, Specialized Medical can follow operational indicators such as monitor battery, electrode contact and quality, monitor-to-phone connection, phone-to-network connection and successful ECG data receipt. When a supported technical issue is identified, the team can contact the patient and help troubleshoot.

Operational test-status visibility is separate from clinical notification. Holter and longer Holter findings are presented after the final report is generated. Qualifying Cardiac Event Monitoring and Mobile Cardiac Telemetry findings may be presented during the study according to the ordering physician's prescribed notification protocol, followed by a final report.

Live ECG monitoring does not mean that one dedicated person manually watches every heartbeat continuously. It does not replace 911, emergency medical services, physician judgment or the treating physician's emergency instructions.

The assigned phone supports five cellular networks (AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon in the United States; Telcel and AT&T Mexico in Mexico) and is configured as a monitoring gateway rather than a general-purpose smartphone.

## Cardiology-practice program facts

- The program supports implementation, user configuration, role-based training, patient enrollment, monitoring operations, patient support, report delivery and physician review.
- Supported workflows include Holter, Long-Term Holter, Extended Holter, Cardiac Event Monitoring and Mobile Cardiac Telemetry.
- Operational live-status visibility is distinct from clinical notification.
- Multi-location programs can organize users, inventory, enrollment, support and report routing by location or centrally.
- The physician retains responsibility for the prescribed test, notification protocol, final interpretation and signature.
- Specialized Medical does not guarantee reimbursement, universal EMR integration, diagnosis or clinical outcomes.

## Ambulatory cardiac monitoring service model

- Nationwide service area: United States.
- Primary featured equipment: compact dual-disk S-Patch Monitoring System.
- Program support includes study setup, live operational oversight for live-streaming configurations, proactive technical support, patient support, and physician-ready reporting.
- Test selection, duration, clinical interpretation, and notification protocols remain subject to the ordering physician's prescription and applicable clinical requirements.

## S-Patch facts

- S-Patch is a compact dual-disk wearable ECG monitoring system with one thin connecting lead.
- Stated weight: 0.6 oz.
- Current validated battery specification: minimum 10 days per battery (one battery is not stated to last 30 days).
- Single-lead ECG; Bluetooth connection to the monitoring phone; symptom logging on the phone.
- IP55 dust and splash resistance; IP55 is not a waterproof rating. Electrodes are repositioned only according to approved patient instructions.
- Prescribed wear: up to 30 days, with battery handling under the support workflow.
- Supported study paths include Holter, Long-Term Holter, Extended Holter, Cardiac Event Monitoring and Mobile Cardiac Telemetry.
- Supported live workflows use a dedicated cellular phone for ECG transmission and operational test-status visibility.
